summary.oneLiner: R&D-driven Indian telecom and networking equipment company delivering high-performance wireline and wireless networking solutions ("Designed and Made in India for the World") to customers in 75+ countries.
summary.business: Tejas Networks designs, develops and manufactures wireless and wireline telecom and networking equipment spanning 4G/5G radio access and core, optical transmission (DWDM/PTN/OTN), broadband access (GPON/XGS-PON), carrier switching and routing (Ethernet/IP-MPLS), broadcast and SAT-IoT solutions. It sells to telecom operators, internet service providers, utilities, wholesale carriers, defense and government organizations worldwide, and also provides network installation, maintenance, upgrade and optimization support services.

currentContext.strengths: R&D-driven organisation with approximately 68% of workforce employed in R&D|Ranked among the top-10 global suppliers in the optical aggregation and optical line terminal markets (source: Omdia)|Large IP portfolio: 676 global patents filed and 371 granted as of FY26 year-end|"Designed and Made in India for the World" positioning aligned with India's telecom self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) policy push, PLI and RDI incentives|Deployed over one million software-defined hardware systems in 500+ carrier networks across 75 countries since inception|Strategic partnerships with Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), NEC Corporation and Rakuten Symphony supporting global go-to-market and joint technology development|Domestic supplier of optical and data networking products for government projects of national/security importance, including national knowledge networks and defense networks|Active contributor to global 5G/6G standards bodies (TSDSI, Bharat 6G Alliance, ITU-R, 3GPP, TIP, O-RAN Alliance)
currentContext.strategies: Industry-leading Portfolio: sustained R&D investment to cater to an AI-powered world - evolving sophisticated 5G-Advanced/6G radios with higher uplink capacities, optical products supporting 1.6 Tbps and beyond per channel for AI data-center interconnect, multi-terabit IP routers, and advanced edge products with integrated access, backhaul and compute for real-time AI inferencing.|Using Partnerships to enhance global Go-to-Market: diversifying the customer base through strong partnerships and alliances, further leveraging the Rakuten Symphony and NEC partnerships to expand global footprint.|Investing in Next-generation Technologies: embracing and investing in 6G and AI to remain at the forefront of technology and standards development; active contribution to global 6G standards via TSDSI, Bharat 6G Alliance, ITU and 3GPP (180+ 3GPP contributions in FY26 alone).|Driving Operational Efficiency: accelerating process automation, quality and cost optimization across R&D, Supply Chain Management and Network Services; forging partnerships across the manufacturing value chain for a resilient and agile supply chain.|Human capital strategy: strengthening people foundations - capabilities, systems, culture and governance - including continued campus hiring pipeline and rollout of Oracle HRMS for data integrity and process standardization.|Continuing to invest in technology leadership, R&D, sustainability and global market expansion to keep products and services differentiated.|The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy sets out the external and internal factors and financial parameters the Board considers in determining dividend distribution, the circumstances in which shareholders may or may not expect a dividend, and how retained earnings are to be utilized. During FY26 the Policy was amended to additionally provide for declaration of dividend in years of exceptional gains or other events.
currentContext.expansion: Under BharatNet Phase-3, Tejas Networks (with the relevant Project Implementation Agencies) will deploy nearly 60,000 of its indigenously designed TJ1400 family of next-generation routers across nine states and five union territories (including Ladakh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Goa, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman & Diu, Puducherry, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Manipur), forming one of the largest indigenous router deployments in India. The company is also expanding its international footprint through customer wins and deployments - a DWDM network expansion for a Southeast Asian Internet & Cloud Service Provider, a multi-country (three-country) optical transport network for a major global sporting event, backhaul capacity upgrades for Vodafone Idea Ltd across multiple circles using TJ1400/TJ1600 platforms, an upgrade of a Pan-African optical backbone for a wholesale connectivity provider, network infrastructure modernization for a Southeast Asian state-owned power utility, and fibre access (OLT) scaling for a global telecom service provider.
currentContext.mdna: AI is catalyzing a new infrastructure super-cycle in telecom networks, reshaping network architecture with real-time edge inferencing, and accelerating adoption of higher-speed technologies (5G-Advanced, 50G PON, 800G/1.2Tbps/1.6Tbps coherent optical) - a direct demand driver for the company's optical, wireless and routing portfolio.|Hyperscaler and AI data-center build-outs are driving terabit-scale data-center interconnect (DCI) demand and a super-cycle of optical network investment; AI-powered apps are also increasing uplink traffic, triggering 4G/5G network densification and offload.|The global (ex-China) addressable market for the company's wireless and wireline products is estimated to grow from US$47 billion to US$55 billion over the next five years.|Government of India's BharatNet Phase III rural broadband rollout (reaching towards ~700,000 villages) is a key demand driver; the company is one of the largest router OEMs on the program.|India's push for technology sovereignty in telecom (Atmanirbhar Bharat, PLI, Telecommunications Act 2023, RDI Fund) favors domestic R&D-led equipment makers such as Tejas.|Structural shift toward open, disaggregated RAN/Core architecture (O-RAN) and growing preference among telecom operators for trusted, locally manufactured equipment amid geopolitical tensions favors alternative vendors like Tejas.|Utility network modernization (power, railway, oil & gas, public safety) is driving replacement of legacy MSPP-based networks with packet technologies (Carrier Ethernet, MPLS-TP/PTN, IP/MPLS) and 4G/5G wireless, including India's CNPN and Kavach initiatives.|Rising smartphone penetration and mobile data usage are driving Tier-1 operators to upgrade 4G/5G backhaul networks using the company's PTN and WDM products.|AI combined with data-sovereignty regulation is driving a data-center revolution in India, with an estimated five-fold growth in DC capacity over the next five years, boosting demand for high-bandwidth optical backbone equipment.|Revenue mix is shifting toward international markets: India customers (government + private) contributed 84% of FY26 net revenue versus 97% in FY25, while international contributed 16% versus 3% in FY25; management believes the expanded wireless/wireline portfolio and increased investment in direct sales and support resources position the company to grow international revenue in coming years.|FY26 revenue declined versus FY25 mainly because FY25 revenue was inflated by completion of the 100,000-site BSNL 4G project supply, and because award of certain expected projects was delayed during FY26.|Order backlog increased from Rs 1,019 crore at end of FY25 to Rs 1,514 crore at end of FY26 (nearly 49% higher), driven by BharatNet and higher orders from domestic and international customers.|Order inflows during FY26 were higher than revenue execution.|A significant portion of revenue is derived from a small number of customers, which may lead to quarterly fluctuation and seasonality.|Company continues to focus on growing and diversifying its order book through product development and international expansion.

risks.note: MD&A flags 'limited number of large customers' and 'aggressive pricing' as a business risk; mitigation is to diversify markets and expand the portfolio into adjacent opportunities. This concentration is illustrated by a Rs 1,335 crore advance received from TCS as part of the 4G project, which will unwind against receivables only as project milestones are completed.
Demand variations and economic downturns are flagged as an industry-level risk that can affect order flow; the stated mitigation is expanding geographical footprint and target markets.

Rapid technological change and the company's ability to keep pace is flagged as a risk; mitigation is actively tracking technology evolution and contributing to global standards bodies (TSDSI, 3GPP, ITU, etc.).

risks.risk: Supply chain / EMS and component supplier concentration
risks.note: Limited availability of EMS (electronics manufacturing services) partners and component suppliers is flagged as a supply-chain risk under the company's asset-light, EMS-partner-based manufacturing model; mitigation is diversifying the EMS and supplier base.

As an R&D-driven organisation with roughly 68% of its workforce in R&D, the ability to attract and retain highly skilled telecom/deep-tech talent is flagged as an operational risk; mitigated via HR best practices, skill development and competitive compensation.

risks.risk: Financial market risk and rising leverage
risks.note: The company is subject to credit, interest-rate and forex risks under its risk-management framework; borrowings increased in FY26 primarily to fund working capital for large project execution, and the company also carries Rs 916 crore of long-term borrowings mainly to fund capex requirements.

The company faces legal and tax proceedings customary for its business, plus the risk of patent-related disputes; mitigation is contesting outstanding proceedings in appropriate forums and continuing to invest in patent filings while monitoring the market for unauthorized use of its products or IP.

one-line thesis: Tejas delivered strong wireless deployment milestones (97.5K BSNL 4G sites, 64T64R 5G radio launch) but faced a Rs. 190cr inventory/warranty write-down distorting Q2 PAT; the core business momentum remains intact with global POCs and BharatNet wins, positioning it for recovery as BSNL's Rs. 1,500cr PO materializes.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +30% QoQ to Rs. 262cr; EBITDA/margin: -394cr EBIT (adjusted: -205cr); PAT (rptd): -307cr (incl. Rs. 190cr one-off provisions); PAT (normalized): -117cr; Order book: Rs. 1,200cr (down from Rs. 1,241cr); Net debt: Rs. 4,166cr (up due to inventory/receivables)
guidance: Revenue growth: No specific guidance; Margin: No guidance, but international projects have higher margins; Order inflow: Expect BSNL Rs. 1,500cr PO in FY26; Capex/commissioning: Capex for product ramp-up ongoing, no specific capex number disclosed
order book & pipeline: Rs. 1,200cr (93% India, 7% international); includes pending BSNL Rs. 1,500cr PO not yet converted to PO
segment / subsidiary detail: Wireless: 97,500 BSNL 4G sites live; 64T64R 5G radio launched; 5G POCs in South Asia and coal mine; O-RAN partnerships with NEC/Rakuten; Wireline: BharatNet Phase-3 wins; 1.2Tbps DWDM launched; 400G/800G wins in India, Europe, Africa; 10G CPON deployed in Europe; SDR: SL3000 chip integrated in smartphones/laptops for D2M
growth verticals / optionality: Global 5G/O-RAN expansion (Africa, LatAm, Asia); AI data center interconnect demand; 6G standardization leadership (India govt. initiative); D2M ecosystem via SL3000 chip adoption
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins not disclosed; profitability of projects is positive on a normalized basis; recent losses driven by Rs. 145cr inventory obsolescence (contract manufacturing losses, design changes) and Rs. 44cr warranty provisions; no recurring large write-offs expected
capex / expansion: Capex incurred to ramp up product portfolio (wireless/wireline); no specific capex amount disclosed; funding sourced via borrowings
capital allocation: Prioritizing R&D (39 patents filed in Q2, 587 total), inventory build for anticipated orders, and working capital for receivables; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt used for capex and working capital
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on product POCs and international conversions; delay in BSNL PO issuance; prolonged high inventory/receivables impacting cash flow; competitive pressure from global vendors (Nokia, Ericsson, Cisco); supply chain disruptions
management quality / tone: Bullish on long-term growth drivers (5G/6G, AI backhaul, D2M); confident in product competitiveness; transparent on challenges but avoids quarter-level guidance; acknowledges investor frustration on disclosures but reiterates policy of no forward numbers
non-obvious takeaways: Tejas is one of only two Indian firms (alongside Tata Elxsi) with a full 4G/5G stack; SL3000 SDR chip integration into consumer devices creates a unique D2M ecosystem moat; BSNL network is the world's largest single-vendor 4G rollout
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSNL's delayed PO issuance | Nokia | loser | Medium | If Tejas captures BSNL PO, it reduces Nokia's share in India's public sector 5G rollout |
| Tejas's SDR chip integration in smartphones | Jio | beneficiary | High | Tejas's D2M tech enables Jio to launch direct-to-mobile TV services without app dependency |

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
